# RunService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("RunService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Provides the events of the frame loop and the simulation clock. Each frame, `PreRender` fires at the frame rate with a variable time step. Each simulation tick, `PreAnimation`, `PreSimulation`, `PostSimulation` and `Heartbeat` fire, in that order, at the fixed tick rate. Use `PreRender` for work tied to the picture and the others for simulation work.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Platform` | `Enum.Platform` | — | read-only | The operating system this machine runs: `Windows`, `Linux`, `MacOS`, `Android` or `IOS`. On a dedicated server, it is the server's operating system. |
| `SimTime` | `number` | — | read-only | The simulation time at the current tick, in seconds. It is constant during a tick and advances by `PhysicsService.FixedTimestep` between ticks. It stops while the world is paused.<br><br>Simulation code should use this clock. `os.clock` measures real time and is only for profiling. |
| `TimeDilation` | `number` | — | read-only | How fast this world's clock runs against the wall's: 1 at full speed, less while an overloaded server is slowed (`[server] time_dilation` in `project.toml`). The tick is the same, so `dt` and what a tick does do not change; fewer ticks run a second, and every machine in the match runs at the same rate. `task.wait`, animations and sounds driven by the simulation slow with it; the interface, the camera and `os.time` do not. `TimeDilationChanged` fires when it changes. |

## Methods

### `BindToIntent(name: string, fn: (intent: IntentWriter) -> (), player: Player? = nil)`

Binds a function that runs as `fn(intent)` on every simulation tick, just after this machine's input has become its player's intents. Use it for input that is not an `InputAction`, such as a turn computed from the mouse, a touch gesture or a bot.

`intent:Set(action, value)` sets an intent by name to a boolean, a number, a `Vector2` or a `vector`. Every reader of `Player:GetIntent` sees the value, on this machine and, in a match, on the authority. A value set this way overrides an `InputAction` of the same name. The `intent` object is valid only during the call.

The optional `player` argument selects a local guest; with nil, the primary local player is used. A binding for a guest that has been removed is skipped. Functions run in the order they were bound. Binding a name that is already bound replaces the function, and a binding belongs to the script that made it and is removed with that script's scene.

### `BindToPredictedStep(name: string, fn: (step: PredictedStep) -> ())`

Binds a function that runs as `fn(step)` inside the simulation step, before physics is solved. It runs once for each player character this machine simulates: every character on the authority, and the client's own on a client. Use it for movement that a script controls and a client should predict without correction at any latency, such as a dash, a double jump, a dodge or a jump pad.

What the function does to the character is part of the step: calling `Move` or `Jump`, or setting a velocity, an impulse, a position or an attribute. When a client is corrected and simulates its character again, the function runs again for each replayed tick, with the input of that tick, and `step.Replaying` is true.

Read the player's input from `step` with `GetIntent` and `Pressed`, and measure time with `step.Tick`, the player's own tick number, which is the same on the client and the authority. An attribute the function sets on `step.Character` is predicted state: it is saved every tick, restored before a tick is replayed, and corrected by the authority's value. Use `step.Random` for random numbers, never an unseeded `Random`.

The function must not yield; `task.wait` inside it raises an error. Functions run in the order they were bound. Binding a name that is already bound replaces the function, and a binding belongs to the script that made it and is removed with that script's scene. In a single-player game the function runs once per tick and is never replayed.

### `BindToRenderStep(name: string, priority: number, fn: (dt: number) -> ())`

Binds a function that runs as `fn(dt)` on every drawn frame, where `dt` is the time since the last frame. In a headset whose runtime makes every other frame (`XRService.SpaceWarp`), that is half the display's rate, with twice the `dt`. Use it for a camera that follows something: inside the function, `GetRenderCFrame` returns where things are drawn, and a camera set there is drawn exactly as set.

Bound functions run in order of `priority`, lowest first, and in the order they were bound when priorities are equal. They run after the input that the frame reads for contexts with `Rate = Render`, and before `PreRender` fires. `Enum.RenderPriority` provides reference values: `Enum.RenderPriority.Camera.Value + 1` runs just after the camera.

Binding a name that is already bound replaces the function. Nothing runs in a run without a window. A binding belongs to the script that made it and is removed with that script's scene.

### `GetLastRun(): { Outcome: Enum.RunOutcome, ScriptErrors: number, FirstScriptError: string?, Report: string?, Dump: string? }`

Returns how the previous run of the game ended on this machine, and where its report is. Call it at startup to offer the player a way to send a crash report: the engine uploads nothing and shows nothing by itself.

`Outcome` is `Clean` when the run was asked to end and did, `Crashed` when it ended in a fault, and `None` when there was no previous run. `Unfinished` means it ended without a fault and without being asked to, which is normal on a phone, where the system closes games in the background. `ScriptErrors` is the number of script errors that nothing caught, and `FirstScriptError` is the first of them.

`Report` is the path of a text file written for a run that crashed, was left unfinished or had script errors. The file identifies the game and the engine and holds the crash note and the end of that run's log. It is nil if the run left nothing to report. `Dump` is the crash dump next to it, on a system that writes one.

A typical check is `if last.Outcome == Enum.RunOutcome.Crashed or last.ScriptErrors > 0 then`. On a phone, the file is in the game's own folder, `Android/data/<package>/files`, which a cable or the system's file browser can open without a permission. The result describes this machine and is the same on a host and on a client.

### `IsPaused(): boolean`

Returns whether the world is paused.

### `Pause()`

Pauses the world. The simulation clock stops: `SimTime` stops advancing, and no `task.wait` or `task.delay` timer completes. Rendering and the debug overlay keep running. Pausing a world that is already paused does nothing.

### `RestoreSimulation(state: buffer): boolean`

Restores a state that `SaveSimulation` returned, and returns true. Returns false and changes nothing if the buffer is not a saved simulation, or if the world's simulated parts and characters differ from those the state was saved with because one was created, destroyed or anchored since.

### `Resume()`

Resumes a paused world and its clock. Resuming a world that is running does nothing.

### `SaveSimulation(): buffer`

Returns the current state of the 3D simulation as a buffer, to roll back to later. It holds the physics solver's state and the position and motion of every simulated part and character.

It does not hold which instances exist, their other properties, the 2D layer or script variables. A rollback game keeps its own state alongside and restores both. The result is deterministic: the same world saved on two machines gives the same bytes.

### `StepSimulation()`

Advances the 3D simulation by one fixed tick immediately, without running scripts and without firing `Touched` or `TouchEnded`. Use it to simulate again after `RestoreSimulation`: for each tick to catch up, set that tick's inputs, such as a character's `MoveDirection` or an impulse, and call it once.

### `UnbindFromIntent(name: string)`

Removes the function bound with `BindToIntent` under `name`. Does nothing if no function is bound under that name.

### `UnbindFromPredictedStep(name: string)`

Removes the function bound with `BindToPredictedStep` under `name`. Does nothing if no function is bound under that name.

### `UnbindFromRenderStep(name: string)`

Removes the function bound with `BindToRenderStep` under `name`. Does nothing if no function is bound under that name.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Heartbeat(dt: number)`

Fires at the end of each simulation tick. Passes the fixed tick length, in seconds. It is the usual place for gameplay code that runs every tick and needs the state the tick ended in.

### `PostSimulation(dt: number)`

Fires each simulation tick, immediately after the physics step. Passes the fixed tick length, in seconds.

### `PreAnimation(dt: number)`

Fires at the start of each simulation tick, before animation is evaluated. Passes the fixed tick length, in seconds.

### `PreRender(dt: number)`

Fires every frame before the frame is drawn, after the functions bound with `BindToRenderStep`. Passes the time since the previous frame, in seconds. Its handlers run in a render step: `GetRenderCFrame` returns where things are drawn, and a camera set there is drawn exactly as set. It never fires in a headless run. In a headset whose runtime makes every other frame (`XRService.SpaceWarp`), it fires once a drawn frame: half the display's rate, with a `dt` twice as long.

### `PreSimulation(dt: number)`

Fires each simulation tick, after animation and before the physics step. Passes the fixed tick length, in seconds.

### `TimeDilationChanged()`

Fires when `TimeDilation` changes: an overloaded server slowing its world, or bringing it back to full speed. A game can say so to its players.
